questions.content: Two long parallel wires are at a distance <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.023ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="2.314ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -694 1023 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mn"><use data-c="32" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-32"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(500,0)"><use data-c="1D451" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D451"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> apart. They carry steady equal currents flowing out of the plane of the paper as shown. The variation of the magnetic field <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.717ex" height="1.545ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -683 759 683" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D435" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D435"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> along the line <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="4.599ex" height="1.717ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -759 2032.7 759" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D44B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D44B"></use></g><g data-mml-node="msup" transform="translate(852,0)"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D44B" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D44B"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(936.2,363) scale(0.707)"><use data-c="2032" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-V-2032"></use></g></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> is given by
questions.explanation: The magnetic field varies inversely with the distance for a long conductor. That is, <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.797ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="7.195ex" height="2.753ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -864.9 3180.4 1217" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="1D435" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D435"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(1036.8,0)"><use data-c="221D" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-221D"></use></g><g data-mml-node="TeXAtom" data-mjx-texclass="ORD" transform="translate(2092.6,0)"><g data-mml-node="mfrac"><g data-mml-node="mn" transform="translate(228.1,394) scale(0.707)"><use data-c="31" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-31"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mi" transform="translate(220,-345) scale(0.707)"><use data-c="1D451" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-I-1D451"></use></g><rect width="569.8" height="60" x="120" y="220"></rect></g></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(2902.4,0)"><use data-c="2E" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-2E"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> According to the magnitude and direction shown graph <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: -0.566ex;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="2.891ex" height="2.262ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -750 1278 1000" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mo"><use data-c="28" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-28"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mn" transform="translate(389,0)"><use data-c="31" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-31"></use></g><g data-mml-node="mo" transform="translate(889,0)"><use data-c="29" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-29"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> is the correct one.
